seo.title: U.S. Paint, Pigment & Ink Export FAQ: Tariffs, HS Codes (Ch. 32) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Short answers: is there a tariff on paint, does Canada or China tariff U.S. paint and TiO2, HS codes for paint, ink and caulk, and is paint hazmat (UN1263).
keywords: is there a tariff on paint
does canada have tariffs on us goods

intro: Short answers to real questions people search about exporting U.S. paint, titanium dioxide, dyes, caulk and printing ink, each with a link to the page that has the detail.
keyTakeaways: Canada, Mexico and South Korea charge nothing on qualifying U.S. paints, pigments and inks, and the EU has charged nothing on any U.S. Chapter 32 good since July 1, 2026.

China stacks its MFN rate, 2019 counter-tariffs and a 10% extra duty: 42.5% on U.S. solvent paint and 29% on TiO2 pigment without an exclusion; its exclusions end December 31, 2026 and its 24-point suspension January 10, 2027.
Before shipping, check TSCA 12(b) export notices, hazmat rules for flammable paint (UN1263) and ink (UN1210), and the BIS licence needed for Russia and Belarus.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on U.S. paint exported to other countries?
searchedAs: is there a tariff on paint
faqs.answer: In the three biggest markets, no: Canada and Mexico charge nothing on U.S. paint that qualifies for USMCA, and the EU has charged nothing on U.S. paints and varnishes since July 1, 2026 (6.5% before). China charges the most — 42.5% on U.S. solvent-based paint and 32.5% on water-based paint without an exclusion. Brazil charges 14%, India 10% and Japan 3.2%–4%.

faqs.question: Does Canada have tariffs on U.S. paint, pigments or ink?
searchedAs: does canada have tariffs on us goods
did canada put tariffs on us goods
faqs.answer: No. Neither Canada's March 2025 counter-tariff list nor its September 8, 2026 list includes any Chapter 32 item, so U.S. paints, pigments, caulks and inks that qualify for CUSMA still enter free. Canada is the largest buyer, at $2.34B in 2025.

faqs.question: What tariff does China charge on U.S. titanium dioxide and paint?
faqs.answer: China stacks three layers: its MFN rate, its 2019 counter-tariffs and a 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods. U.S. TiO2 pigment (3206.1110) pays 29% (6.5% + 10% + 2.5% + 10%) and solvent paint (3208.90) 42.5%; a buyer holding an exclusion, valid to December 31, 2026, pays only the MFN rate plus 10%. U.S. exports to China fell 21.6% to $289M in 2025.

faqs.question: When could China's tariffs on U.S. paint and pigments go up?
faqs.answer: Two dates: China's exclusions from its 2019 counter-tariffs end December 31, 2026, and the suspension of 24 points of its extra duty ends January 10, 2027. If the suspension lapses, the extra duty goes from 10% to 34%, taking U.S. solvent paint from 42.5% to 66.5% without an exclusion.

faqs.question: Does Mexico charge tariffs on U.S. paint and pigments?
searchedAs: does mexico have tariffs on us goods
does mexico charge tariffs on us goods
faqs.answer: Not on goods that qualify for USMCA, which enter free. Without a USMCA certification of origin Mexico's MFN rates apply, for example 9% on TiO2 pigment and 10% on artists' colors, and Mexico's December 2025 tariff increases did not touch Chapter 32. Paints and inks sold in Mexico need Spanish labelling under NOM-003-SSA1-2006.

faqs.question: What tariff does the EU charge on U.S. paint, pigments and ink?
faqs.answer: None since July 1, 2026: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 lists all of Chapter 32 and zeroes the EU's duties of up to 6.5% on U.S.-origin goods until December 31, 2029, on proof of U.S. origin. The EU's suspended 2025 countermeasure list would have added 30% to most U.S. paints, dyes and inks.

faqs.question: What is the HS or Schedule B code for paint?
faqs.answer: Paints and varnishes are heading 3208 when solvent-based (3208.90 for epoxies, polyurethanes and other polymers, $877M of 2025 exports) and 3209 when water-based (3209.10 for acrylic or vinyl latex paint, $760M). The 10-digit Schedule B number starts with those six digits; look it up with the Census Schedule B search tool.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for printing ink?
faqs.answer: Printing ink is heading 3215: 3215.11 for black and 3215.19 for other colors (the largest ink line, $405M of 2025 U.S. exports), and 3215.90 for writing, drawing and other inks.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for titanium dioxide pigment?
searchedAs: hs code for titanium dioxide pigment
faqs.answer: Pigments and preparations with 80% or more titanium dioxide are 3206.11 ($873M of 2025 U.S. exports, down 18.4%); those with less are 3206.19. Titanium dioxide as a chemical (HS 2823) belongs to Chapter 28, not Chapter 32.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for caulk and sealant?
faqs.answer: Caulks, glazier's putty, resin cements and painters' fillings are 3214.10, the largest single Chapter 32 export line at $932M in 2025; non-refractory surfacing preparations for walls and floors are 3214.90.

faqs.question: Is paint a hazardous material for shipping?
searchedAs: is paint considered hazardous material for shipping
faqs.answer: Flammable solvent-based paints, varnishes and driers usually are: they ship as Class 3 dangerous goods under UN1263 (Paint or Paint related material), and solvent-based printing inks under UN1210, following DOT's Hazardous Materials Regulations (49 CFR 172.101). Water-based latex paint is usually not flammable; check the safety data sheet.

faqs.question: How much paint and pigment does the U.S. export, and who buys it?
faqs.answer: U.S. Chapter 32 exports were $7.78B in 2025, down 4.1%, of which paints and varnishes were $2.80B and TiO2 and other pigments $1.48B. Canada ($2.34B) and Mexico ($1.66B) buy 51%, followed by the EU ($898M), South Korea ($355M) and China ($289M).
